Hi, I'm Nico.

Nicolas Perez Diaz

18. From Cancún, Mexico. Based in Ubud, Bali.

1,200+videos since age 6
90+podcast episodes
60M+subs on my biggest guest's channel
400+hours assisting yoga trainings
15+countries in two years

When I started my YouTube channel at six, my dad helped me create the account and upload my first video. Then he told me to "figure it out." So I did. Since then, I haven't stopped building stuff. Eleven years and 1,200+ videos later, that's millions of views and several channels past 10,000 subscribers.

my first video

Since then: 1,200+ videos. Each square is one.

At 8, I sold print-on-demand shirts and made $200.

At 9, I started running multiple Minecraft servers. At 11, I saw my brother listening to a podcast and thought it looked fun. That same day, I recorded my very first episode, with him as my first guest. Then I started cold-emailing people. As I was experimenting with email subject lines, I wondered who was the world's youngest podcaster. I did some research and the most official media site I could find claimed a 13-year old was the world's youngest podcaster. But I was 11! So "The World's Youngest Podcaster" became my best performing email subject. Since then, I've done 90+ episodes on my podcast, Nicocast, with guests like IShowSpeed (his first interview ever, back when he had around 4M subscribers; he now has 60M+), Yes Theory (10M+), and Jamie Rawsthorne, one of the Academy's mentors, amongst many other top creators, company founders, VCs, top Mexican actors, and people who like to think differently and dream big.

yes, really.

I keep catching people right before they blow up. The podcast is making a comeback soon, with the first Season 2 guests already booked.

When YouTube Shorts launched, I started Minecraft and Roblox Shorts channels that grew to 50K subscribers, until YouTube deleted them, thinking I'd bought the subscribers. I hadn't. They just grew too fast. So I went back to the podcast and doubled down on video editing.

one of my channels, ticking past 15K live (2022)

At 13, I also co-ran a Minecraft Shorts channel with a friend, splitting everything 50/50. We called it MrsBeast. It hit 255K subscribers before it got deleted too.

the receipts

At 12, someone noticed my video editing skills and I started getting freelance jobs. Referral after referral, I started editing for some bigger brands like MSCHF and Studio.com, all before I was even a teenager. I started my own production company and I started hiring some freelancers myself on Upwork for some of the jobs.

At 14, I had a conversation with my British neighbor at the time about medicine and his business. I mentioned a few suggestions, and soon after, I had another job. I helped him with videos and I wrote articles focused on medical and business terms.

All along, I'd also been making iOS apps, websites, and other side projects during school hours, Frankensteining code together from Stack Overflow long before AI coding tools existed, and installing questionable .jar files for Minecraft mods. One of those side projects was a games website. My school blocked online games so I figured out how to unblock the school system. One day I came back from the bathroom and everyone in my English class was playing on my website.

true story

That year, ChatGPT had just come out. Around the same time, I watched an old Steve Jobs talk where he imagines a computer that lets you ask Aristotle a question. So I built it: I learned SwiftUI and shipped Ask Aristotle, an iOS app where you can talk to him, running on ChatGPT's brand-new API. It got a couple hundred downloads without me promoting it at all, and an app studio offered to buy it for $1K. I said no. They wanted way too much for that price.

At 15, I started Project Goat, a newsletter about travel, experiences, and ideas. I wrote it every single week for two years. It's not weekly anymore, but it's still going (start with the one on luck).

I realized I had been learning more outside of school than in school.

Even though I was Class President for the 3rd consecutive year at my school, I decided to leave traditional school. I convinced my parents to rent our house in Mexico and travel the world, one month in each country, while I did a self-paced online program. So my mom, dad, and I left Cancún in August 2024 and started traveling full-time. We called this "Project Goat", since goats adapt to all environments. I've been documenting the whole journey in my youtube channel and newsletter. We've been to 15+ countries (about 2-10 weeks each) in the past two years.

One of those stops was India, and that's where I started doing yoga. I had never done it before. My parents were doing a Nada Yoga training in Rishikesh, we'd be there about a month, and I figured I might as well do something too. So I signed up for a 200-hour Hatha Yoga Teacher Training. I had no idea it would become a major part of my life.

graduating my first training, Rishikesh

After five weeks in Rishikesh, I traveled up into Uttarakhand toward Gangotri, near the source of the Ganges. From there I kept traveling while finishing high school, making videos, writing, and freelancing.

I kept coming back to yoga.

In Kenya, I taught yoga, English, and writing at a juvenile detention center. In Laos, I assisted with English classes. In India, I translated at yoga retreats.

teaching English in Kenya
cropped to protect my students' privacy

In Bali, I joined a 200-hour Power Vinyasa training after the lead teacher gave me a scholarship and a role as trainee assistant. Since then I've kept getting invited back, and I've now assisted 400+ hours of teacher trainings with Paul Teodo, Kimberly Utama, and Emily Kuser.

graduating the training I assisted, with my teachers
teaching my own class, Ubud 2025
teaching pranayama, in Spanish

At 17, I graduated high school a year early, while traveling through 15+ countries, freelancing, making videos, and assisting 400+ hours of yoga teacher trainings.

That was September 2026. A few days later, I turned 18.

Now

I'm based in Ubud, Bali, after two years of traveling. I assist yoga teacher trainings and I'm building Yoga with Nico. I'm relaunching Nicocast for Season 2, recording with the first guests this month. On the side, I'm building Respira with my mom, a breathwork platform for Spanish speakers.

Why the Academy

I've wanted something like this for as long as I can remember. Since I was a kid, I've been looking up people who skipped college or dropped out to build things, looking for proof there was another way. This program is exactly what I was looking for, and I want it so bad.

For years, almost everyone around me has been older than me: clients, yoga teachers, podcast guests, even my friends. I'd love to finally build with people my own age.

And in San Francisco, one of the first things I'd do is start running yoga sessions at startups and companies, and bring everything I've learned to the people who need it most.
